records.title: Stati di aggregazione
records.derivation: Density definition rho=m/V gives V=m/rho. For each assigned state use its own given density, not a universal density inferred from its phase name. Transfer at state2 (Liquido) uses6g and yields6/rho_liquid cm3 if density is in g/cm3. The first assignment at state3 cannot be numeric without model mass and gas density.
records.domain: Control is discrete1,2,3, not continuous phase interpolation. Same mass is specified for the comparison. Assigned phase densities are model data; no universal monotonic solid/liquid/gas density law or thermodynamic transition path is inferred.
records.manual: Divide the given mass by the state-specific density; g cancels g in g/cm3. Numerical manual work remains pending until model mass/density table is legitimately read.

records.title: Fluidi e solidi
records.derivation: For stationary plane Couette flow, u(z)=U*z/d under no slip. Newtonian shear tau=eta*du/dz=eta*U/d. With eta1Pa s,d2cm,U=xcm/s, tau=x/2Pa. First6cm/s gives3Pa; transfer4cm/s gives2Pa.
records.domain: U0..8cm/s; nonnegative shear magnitude. Parallel stationary lower plate and uniformly moving upper plate; incompressible Newtonian constant viscosity, linear developed profile/no pressure gradient. Startup is not automatically this steady profile.
records.manual: The same centimetres cancel in U/d, leaving s^-1. Multiply by1Pa s and divide by2. Zero speed giveszero stress. Fluids sustain steady shear by continuous deformation; an elastic solid may sustain static shear.
pending: whether student-delivered context states steady linear Newtonian profile rather than arbitrary startup

records.title: Densità
records.derivation: Uniform material mass m=rho V. rho=5/2g/cm3, xcm3 gives(5/2)xg. First6cm3 gives15g; transfer5cm3 gives25/2g=12.5g.
records.domain: V1..8cm3; same uniform density, content mass excluding container tare. Density2500kg/m3 is material property here, not mass or apparent weight.
records.manual: Multiply volume by5, then halve; units cm3 cancel. Use the contents only, not the tube mass.

records.title: Pressione e forza normale
records.derivation: Mean normal contact pressure p=F_perp/A. A=x*10^-4m2,F10N yields100000/xPa=100/xkPa. First5cm2 gives20kPa; transfer7cm2 gives100/7kPa.
records.domain: Positive area1..10cm2; total normal load10N fixed. Mean pressure formula does not prove uniform local pressure or shear-normal equality.
records.manual: 1cm2=(1/100m)^2=1/10000m2; divide Pa by1000 for kPa. 100/7=14+2/7=14.285714...;100000=7*14285+5 supports decimal by long division. Entering14.286 gives relativeerror1/50000; actual grader tolerance still to inspect.

records.title: Pressione assoluta e relativa
records.derivation: Open stationary liquid: dp/dz=-rho*g. At depth1m, p_abs=p_atm+rho*g*(1m). In kPa output is x+rho*g/1000 (rho SI,g SI). First100kPa and transfer90kPa become110 and100kPa ONLY IF assigned rho1000kg/m3 andg10m/s2. Relative pressure at that depth is independent of atmosphere.
records.domain: Atmosphere70..110kPa; open surface, same liquid density and uniform g, depth held1m. Absolute zero refers to vacuum; relative pressure references surface atmospheric pressure.
records.manual: Add the same hydrostatic increment to each atmospheric value. Do not replace rho*g by10000Pa/m until actual assigned constants are read.

records.title: Legge di Stevino
records.derivation: Sensor zeroed at surface measures rho*g*h. Assigned g10m/s2, h=xm. If water density1000kg/m3 is assigned, output10xkPa: first2m20kPa, transfer3/2m15kPa.
records.domain: Depth0..3m measured downward from free surface, static constant-density liquid, constantg10. Zero depth giveszero relative pressure, notzero absolute pressure.
records.manual: Multiply depth byrho*10 and divide by1000. Withrho1000 this reduces to10x. Column-area cancels:rho*A*h*g/A.

records.title: Pressione con la profondità
records.derivation: Quota z abovebottom differs from depth. With surface quota3m, h=3-z. Relativep=rho*g*(3-z). In kPa outputrho*g*(3-x)/1000. Withrho1000,g10, firstz2m gives10kPa; transferz3/2m gives15kPa.
records.domain: z0..3m; uniform static liquid andg. Pressure decreases upward, derivative-rho*g; top boundary relative0. No negative pressures inside this assigned interval.
records.manual: Subtract selected quota from3 before multiplying. Never substitute quota itself for depth. Constants remain conditional until delivered context is read.

records.title: Esperimento di Torricelli
records.derivation: Balance on a stationary barometer column with negligible top-vapor pressure gives p_air=rho*g*h. rho13600kg/m3,g10; h_cm=100*x*1000/136000=(25/34)x. First102kPa gives75cm; transfer442/5kPa=88.4 gives65cm.
records.domain: p68..108.8kPa, increments1.36kPa. Ideal vacuum above mercury or vaporpressure explicitly neglected. Nonzero top pressure would require subtraction; tube must be tall enough and surface reference clear.
records.manual: 13600*10=136000; cmconversion reduces multiplier to25/34.102/34=3 ->75;88.4/34=2.6 ->65. Each1.36kPa grid increment corresponds exactly1cm.
pending: actual top-vacuum/vaporpressure assumption and rendered height reference

records.title: Manometro a U
records.derivation: At commonbottomlevel, p_L+rho*g*(H-z_L)=p_R+rho*g*(H-z_R). Thus dp=p_L-p_R=rho*g*(z_R-z_L), so signedright-minus-left height in cm=100000*x/(rho*g) for xkPa. First2kPa gives200000/(rho*g)cm, transfer0 gives0cm. If liquidrho1000,g10 these are20 and0cm, but liquid is not assumed from apparatus name.
records.domain: Signed pressure difference-2..2kPa; one static constant-density manometer liquid, negligible/known gascolumns, equal bottomreference. Equal section area needed only for symmetric displacement of individual levels, not difference formula. Positiveleft excess makes left level lower/right levelhigher.
records.manual: Convert kPa toPa, divide byrho*g to metres, thenmultiply100 forcm; preserve sign. Transfer0 requires no division approximation, both levels equal. Numerical first task remains conditional on material constants.

records.title: Principio di Pascal
records.derivation: Pascal transmits added pressure, not equalforces across unequalareas. DeltaF=DeltaP*Aout. Aout20cm2=1/500m2, xkPa=1000xPa, so DeltaF=2xN. First6kPa gives12N; transfer5kPa gives10N.
records.domain: Addedpressure0..10kPa; confined ideal static incompressible liquid, connected pistons, area fixed20cm2, no unmodeled pressureloss. Hydrostatic baseline differences may exist but same pressureincrement is transmitted.
records.manual: Square the cm conversion:20/10000m2=1/500m2;1000/500=2. Multiply eachpressureincrement by2. This is increment force, nottotal piston force including baseline or mass.
pending: actual piston areas/forceincrement vs total force readout
